paper_title: Socratic Skill Learning: Interleaving Teaching and Practice for Transferable Agent Skills

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Agent Skills improve LLM agents by making task knowledge reusable across sessions. Learning transferable Skills requires evidence about a procedure and its conditions of use, which a successful task attempt can leave untested. We introduce Socratic Skill Learning (SSL), which interleaves expert teaching with Student practice. An Educator guides investigation while the Student remains the sole environment operator and Skill author, able to question, test, and adapt advice. To test reuse beyond the learning task, we construct SkillTransferBench, with 35 task families and 408 executable cases, pairing public variation specifications with held-out evaluation in fresh solver sessions. On the main 22-family, 155-case cohort, Fixed-Window SSL reaches 0.801 utility, versus 0.723 without a Skill, 0.761 for adapted Trace2Skill (trajectory distillation), and 0.751 for adapted SKILL-KD (contrastive distillation). Across three model pairs on shared families, interleaved guidance outperforms expert authoring and post-hoc teaching. Process analysis links guidance to Student writing and package revision; a case study shows the Student testing and refining a proposed procedure for later reuse. As demand for new lessons falls, the cost of fixed-window review grows. Issue-Guided SSL tracks unresolved questions across Skill revisions to select and focus review, reaching 0.805 utility with 61.7% fewer Educator tokens and 16.9% fewer total acquisition tokens than Fixed-Window SSL on the main cohort.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Agent Skills extend LLM agents through reusable instructions and executable resources, without updating model weights (Anthropic, 2025). Curated Skills improve success on tasks requiring specialized expertise (Li et al., 2026b). Acquiring transferable Skills requires identifying which steps to reuse, under what conditions, and when to adapt them. Recent methods distill execution trajectories into Skills and refine packages through testing and feedback (Ni et al., 2026; Ma et al., 2026; Shi et al., 2026). SkillLearnBenchs Teacher Feedback uses expert advice after failed attempts to guide revision (Zhong et al., 2026). Such refinement depends on which hypotheses the learner tests and which failures it investigates. Guidance during an ongoing attempt can redirect these choices before an untested assumption becomes reusable rule. We therefore ask: how should external expertise guide the learner while it is still gathering evidence? We introduce Socratic Skill Learning (SSL), interleaving expert teaching with Student practice (Figure 3).1 An Educator observes recent Student work and the live Skill, then explains, challenges, diag1Code, benchmark, and trajectories: project repository. 1 / 25 noses, or remains silent. The Student operates the environment and authors the package. Inspired by Socratic inquiry, the interaction examines assumptions through dialogue and practical checks; the Student can question advice, adapt it, and decide what to retain. We instantiate SSL with FIXED-WINDOW SSL, which reviews at regular tool-call intervals, and ISSUE-GUIDED SSL, which focuses review on unresolved learning issues. Socratic Skill Learning Figure 1. Overview of the study. Panels show (A) task-family construction from six source benchmarks, (B) acquisition-protocol comparisons, external methods, and model pairs, and (C) the path from teaching demand to issue-guided review with utility and cost. Panel summarizes Qwen experiments on the 22-family main cohort. Existing benchmarks measure Skill utility and reuse (Li et al., 2026b; Zhong et al., 2026). Studying guided acquisition also requires specifying what the learner should investigate beyond the practice task. We construct SKILLTRANSFERBENCH, benchmark of 35 task families and 408 executable cases across six domains. Each family pairs an anchor task with public specification of invariants and permitted variation. This specification guides exploration; fresh solvers test the acquired package on held-out family members. We organize the study around four questions (Figure 1): RQ1: How well does SSL transfer relative to existing induction methods? RQ2: How should external expertise guide Skill acquisition? RQ3: How does guidance enter Skill development as learning progresses? RQ4: How should review be organized to sustain transfer with less expert supervision? On shared families across three model pairs, both interleaved protocols outperform direct expert authoring and post-hoc teaching. Process analysis links lessons to Student development; case study shows the Student testing an Educator-proposed procedure and refining it for later reuse. ISSUE-GUIDED SSL reaches 0.805 utility with 61.7% fewer Educator tokens on the main cohort. 2 / Socratic Skill Learning Our contributions are threefold: We construct SKILLTRANSFERBENCH, containing 35 task families and 408 executable cases across six domains, with public family specifications that guide acquisition and held-out evaluation that tests frozen Skills in fresh solver sessions. We introduce Socratic Skill Learning (SSL), in which the Student owns exploration, verification, and Skill authoring while an Educator guides practice. Issue-Guided SSL uses persistent learning issues to select and focus review around unresolved questions. We evaluate Skill transfer across three model pairs and complement these comparisons with process analysis and case studies, linking guidance to Student development and showing how selecting and focusing review sustains transfer with less expert supervision.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Constructing Skills from execution evidence. Skills can retain experience as guidance or executable code (Zhao et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2023), consolidate trajectory lessons (Ni et al., 2026), or evolve through execution and verification (Ma et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2026b). SKILL-KDs consolidation agent derives patches from TeacherStudent trajectory contrasts and validates them through Student reruns (Shi et al., 2026). Feedback during Skill development. Self-Refine and Reflexion improve outputs or attempts through feedback (Madaan et al., 2023; Shinn et al., 2023). For agent diagnosis (Zhao et al., 2026), CodeTracer reconstructs state transitions to localize failures (Li et al., 2026a). SkillLearnBench uses reference Skill to guide revision after failure (Zhong et al., 2026); AgentBrew validates teacher-authored corrections through student retries (Jiang and Huang, 2026). HASP includes teacher review of student-proposed skill programs (Liu et al., 2026a), while SkillHone preserves revision evidence and decisions (Li and Hu, 2026). SSL places Educator guidance within Student investigation and verification, leaving the Student to author the Skill. Unresolved learning questions select and focus review. This design connects Socratic dialogue (Liu et al., 2024a) with learner construction (Chi et al., 2001) and feedback on the learning process (Hattie and Timperley, 2007). Scope and transfer in Skill evaluation. SkillsBench measures Skill utility (Li et al., 2026b); SkillLearnBench and EconSkills evaluate reuse across parameterized instances (Zhong et al., 2026; Quan and Liu, 2026). Trace2Skill tests held-out transfer (Ni et al., 2026), while ContinualSkillBench uses ordered task streams (Guan et al., 2026). SKILLTRANSFERBENCH defines acquisition scope through public family specification. Across six domains, evaluation in fresh sessions connects guided acquisition to held-out transfer and supervision cost.

sections.title: 3.2 Benchmark construction
sections.content: We construct the benchmark in three stages: adapt source tasks, build task families through two complementary routes, and validate the resulting cases. Source adaptation. We select tasks with clear requirements and meaningful variation from six benchmarks: Terminal-Bench and AgentIF-OneDay (Merrill et al., 2026; Chen et al., 2026), SpreadsheetBench (Ma et al., 2024), CodeContests and FullStackBench (Li et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2024b), and OﬀiceBench (Wang et al., 2024). We normalize their formats and align descriptions, fixtures, and scorers. Task-family construction. Experts in coding and agent benchmarking collaborate with agents through two routes (Figure 1A): extraction and adaptation groups compatible source cases under shared specification and aligns their statements and tests; seed expansion starts from one task, defines its invariant goal and permitted variation, and authors additional cases within that scope. Both routes yield public family specification and executable variants. One fixed case serves as the acquisition anchor; the remaining cases provide candidates for held-out evaluation. Validation. Each case includes resettable environment, reference solution, and private tests. Programmatic checks verify Docker builds, execute tests, and confirm that reference solutions pass them; an expert other than the author then reviews each case before acceptance. Reference solutions and private tests remain outside agent workspaces (Appendix B). Catalog and evaluation cohorts. The full catalog contains 35 families and 408 cases across six domains, with 517 cases per family, including the anchor (Figure 2). The main cohort selects families with at least 5 verified held-out cases and at least two non-perfect outcomes in catalog-wide No-Skill screening, yielding 22 families and 155 held-out cases  (Table 5)  ; its lite subset covers 10 families and 77 cases across all six domains for comparisons across model pairs. Each pair independently acquires its own packages. 4 / Socratic Skill Learning

sections.title: 4 Socratic Skill Learning
sections.content: We introduce Socratic Skill Learning (SSL), in which an Educator guides ongoing investigation while Student tests the guidance and authors transferable Skill. We develop two instantiations: FIXED-WINDOW SSL periodically reviews Student progress, while ISSUE-GUIDED SSL maintains learning issues to select and focus subsequent reviews. We first describe their shared learning process (Figure 3A), then present each protocol (Figure 3B). Figure 3. Socratic Skill Learning. (A) The Student tests guidance and authors the Skill; the Educator reviews recent work and the live package read-only. Only the Skill transfers to fresh solvers. (B) FIXED-WINDOW SSL reviews every tool calls; ISSUE-GUIDED SSL reviews unresolved issues when they open, change, or reopen, using focused context. 5 / 25 Socratic Skill Learning

sections.title: 4.1 Socratic dialogue and Student practice
sections.content: Both protocols use the target solvers model as the Student, the sole environment operator and author of K. Guided by the family specification, it explores the anchor, tests candidate procedures, and decides what evidence to gather and what knowledge to retain (Section 3.1). Educator review and Student response. The Educator has read-only access to recent Student work and the live Skill. It can explain, challenge, diagnose, propose checks, or remain silent. The Student can question, test, adapt, or reject advice, responding through dialogue, environment experiments, and package revisions. This interaction examines the assumptions behind procedure and the evidence needed to retain it, with the Student deciding how the evidence changes the Skill. Rounds and transfer. fresh solver tests each rounds package on the reset anchor, checking whether it carries the procedure beyond the authors session. The resulting trajectory and verifier feedback guide the next round. Student and Educator sessions persist; evaluation sessions are fresh. Only the final package transfers to held-out family members.

sections.title: 4.2 Fixed-Window SSL
sections.content: Fixed-Window SSL organizes acquisition as repeated periods of Student practice and Educator review. After every completed Student tool calls, the Educator examines recent reasoning and tool results alongside the live Skill, informed by the family specification, prior lessons, and anchor feedback. This recurring review can challenge an assumption or suggest missing check while an investigation is still open, shaping the evidence gathered before procedure is retained. The Student can clarify or contest lesson, then resumes exploration and Skill revision. The resulting work informs the next review. Silence lets practice continue directly. The schedule thus fixes when review occurs, while guidance responds to the Students progress. The Student determines when to finish the round; final review covers any work since the previous review, allowing Student action before the snapshot (Appendix C.2).

sections.title: 4.3 Issue-Guided SSL
sections.content: Teaching demand changes as Skill develops: practice can settle question, while new evidence can call for further guidance. Issue-Guided SSL tracks unresolved questions across revisions to select when review is needed and focus it on relevant evidence. Persistent learning issues. An Educator lesson supplies learning focus and an acceptance criterion: what to investigate and what observable evidence would resolve it. learning issue retains these together with evidence and package revisions for subsequent review. Issues form persistent LEARNINGISSUE TREE: concern arising within an investigation becomes child; closing it returns attention to the nearest unresolved ancestor. Resolved branches preserve what has already been addressed. Revisions and resolution. The Student groups file edits into coherent revision, declaring its summary, evidence, and any issue addressed. An addressed issue can close with changed package when the Student verifies the revision, documents the procedures applicability with evidence, or rejects the guidance on evidential grounds. Verified closure requires successful post-lesson check. Investigation can therefore settle question without another Educator call. Selective review and reopening. An initial review occurs at the first revision or after warm-up window of tool calls. Thereafter, an unresolved issue must open, change, or reopen before further review. The Educator receives the active issue and its ancestors, the latest revision, and recent local work, with read access to the complete package. lesson returns the Student to investigation; silence closes the current review episode. Contradictory fresh-solver anchor feedback can reopen the associated issue in the next round while preserving resolved siblings. Appendix C.2 gives event rules and boundary handling. 6 / 25 Socratic Skill Learning

sections.title: 5 Can SSL Develop Transferable Agent Skills?
sections.content: To assess how teaching supports Skill acquisition, we investigate four research questions (RQs): RQ1 evaluates transfer to held-out family members; RQ2 compares how expert guidance is organized across model pairs; RQ3 traces teaching, Student actions, and package revisions during acquisition; and RQ4 examines whether issue-guided review preserves transfer while reducing expert supervision. Evaluations follow the shared protocol in Section 3.

sections.title: 5.2 RQ2: Organizing expert guidance during Skill acquisition
sections.content: How should external expertise guide Skill acquisition? Table 2(a) compares the four authoring protocols on the shared 10 families across the Qwen, DeepSeek, and Kimi model pairs, complemented by the Qwen main cohort. Within each pair, the solver and tasks are fixed; protocols differ in who investigates and writes the package, when guidance is available, and how the agents interact (Appendices and D). Guidance during practice consistently produces stronger transfer than reviewing the Students completed authoring trajectory. Fixed-Window SSL and Post-hoc Teaching both preserve the Student as environment operator and package author, but Fixed-Window SSL outperforms Post-hoc Teaching on all three model pairs. On the main cohort, this advantage is 5.31 percentage points in utility with 21% fewer acquisition tokens. Interleaving lets the Student test advice while an investigation is still open and use 7 / 25 Socratic Skill Learning the resulting evidence in subsequent exploration and writing. Post-hoc review arrives after those earlier choices have shaped the package. The results favor feedback that can redirect evidence gathering throughout practice. The ordering also distinguishes guided practice from simply retaining Student author. sections.title: 6 Discussion and Conclusion
sections.content: On shared SKILLTRANSFERBENCH families across three model pairs, Socratic Skill Learning (SSL) improves transfer over direct expert authoring and post-hoc teaching. Process and case analyses show how guidance enters Skill development: advice identifies direction to investigate, while execution evidence informs how the Student tests, adapts, and retains procedure. As teaching demand changes, unresolved questions provide basis for allocating expert attention. IssueGuided SSL tracks these questions across revisions, retaining transfer utility with 2.75 times the gain per Educator token of Fixed-Window SSL on the main cohort. The study connects the development of reusable knowledge with decisions about where further guidance is needed.

We first convert source tasks to common format, reconciling paths, formats, ordering, precision, and boundary conditions across the task descriptions, fixtures, and scorers. In extraction and adaptation, compatible source cases are grouped into families, and statements and tests are revised to align their requirements. In seed expansion, case from the adapted pool seeds specification of the shared invariant and permitted variation; experts and agents then develop additional cases within this scope. Each task includes description, public fixtures, resettable environment, reference solution, and private verifier. Protocols, Implementation, and Reproduction C.1 Runtime, sessions, and package boundaries Runtime and models. We abbreviate the three model pairs as Qwen, DeepSeek, and Kimi. In each pair, the Student model also serves as the fresh solver, while the Educator model supplies external expertise 14 / 25 Socratic Skill Learning or writes the package under Expert Authoring. The harness uses Pi coding agent 0.81.12, TypeScript 5.9.3, and Docker task environments. Main Qwen runs use qwen3.7-plus as Student and qwen3.7-max as Educator, with 1,000,000-token context window, 65,536-token maximum completion, and thinking enabled. Sampling uses the provider defaults. DeepSeek uses deepseek-v4-flash-0731 as Student and deepseek-v4-pro-0813 as Educator, with the same context window, 393,216 maximum completion tokens, thinking enabled, and reasoning effort max. Kimi uses kimi-k2.5 for the Student and fresh solvers (262,144-token context, 16,384 maximum completion, thinking enabled), and kimi-k3 for the external author or Educator (1,048,576-token context, 131,072 maximum completion, reasoning effort max). Session isolation and access. Within an original authoring-protocol run, the package author (the external model under Expert Authoring; the Student otherwise) and, where applicable, the Educator maintain separate continuous sessions across acquisition rounds, with automatic context compaction. Sessions never continue across families, replicates, or protocol cells. Every anchor and held-out evaluation uses fresh target-model solver. Adapted SKILL-KD instead uses fresh executions with persistent rule-edit history (Appendix C.3.1). The author operates in Docker workspace containing the public task, anchor inputs, and family specification, and is the only agent that writes the live Skill. Educator tools list, read, and search the full package but cannot execute environment actions or write files. Solvers load only the frozen target package through the native Skill catalog, with ambient Skills disabled and clean case workspace. The package contains SKILL.md and optional scripts/, references/, and assets/ directories. Held-out materials remain inaccessible during acquisition, and private checks are applied only after the solver submits its solution. Snapshots retain every package file; resource reads and executable invocations are logged. C.2 Acquisition loop and review events Review context and interaction. FIXED-WINDOW SSL reviews after every completed Student tool calls, with = 10 in the main condition and = 5, 20 in the schedule comparison. FIXED-WINDOW SSL provides the Educator with the family definition, recent reasoning and tool calls, prior lessons, feedback from anchor tests by fresh solvers, and the complete live package. An opening lesson may explain, propose test, diagnose, or challenge an assumption; the Student may clarify, adapt, or contest it, followed by at most one Educator reply. Subsequent task actions and package edits remain Student decisions. Round completion. The author ends its trajectory when it has finished the current exploration and package revision. The harness completes the scheduled terminal review, if any, and the Students resulting work, then validates and snapshots the package for fresh anchor test. Each round permits at most one terminal review; resulting Student work is retained without another terminal review. The tool-call window controls review frequency, while the author determines trajectory length. All 3 rounds run, with anchor feedback entering the next round. Revision declarations and issue state. During practice, the Student calls commit_skill_revision after coherent knowledge change to the complete package. The declaration includes summary and evidence, plus an issue ID and disposition when it addresses an existing lesson. Ordinary file edits accumulate until the Student commits such revision. The Educator supplies learning focus and an observable acceptance criterion when delivering lesson. Each persistent issue stores focus, acceptance criterion, linked revisions, evidence, and disposition. child records concern within ongoing work; closure returns attention to the nearest unresolved ancestor. In Issue-Guided SSL, the first-round bootstrap occurs at the first revision or after ten tool calls, whichever comes first. At the round boundary, an uncommitted package change is processed as an implicit revision; the runtime also handles any pending bootstrap or anchor contradiction before the final snapshot. The default Educator view includes up to three active-path nodes, two recently closed issues, the latest revision, and recent local tool calls; read access to the complete package remains available. These labels describe its intended change in learner state. lesson may receive multiple labels; silence is separate decision. sections.title: H Limitations
sections.content: Our study evaluates complete Skill-learning protocols under shared single-anchor setting. Further controlled comparisons could isolate how much the Educator, review timing, and issue structure each contribute to transfer performance and teaching cost. 25 /
